reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Forsage as a money-oriented matrix requiring viewers to purchase ETH-denominated slots, with participation described as generating wallet payouts. It recommends a 0.35 ETH starting contribution, encourages partners to use the same approach, and associates progression through the structure with a stated return of 1430 ETH or 350,000 dollars. The records do not independently verify the figures or establish completed payments.

citations.quote: How does Forsage marketing work? Forsage marketing is a classic matrix that is the most effective system in terms of money.
When you invite partners they take places under you.
Each subsequent slot is exactly two times more expensive than the previous one. Accordingly, income from them are also twice as high.
The first slot of each program costs 0.025 ETH, but you can not buy them separately. They are bought together at registration.
The first partner takes a place below you, a 100% payout instantly credited to your personal wallet.

opening.argument: The presentation identifies the basis of its security claims rather than asking viewers to trust an unnamed operator: it explains that the contract code is placed on a blockchain, that calculations are distributed across computers, and that there is no central point to hack. It also states that the terms are fixed in the program and that even the creators cannot change them. Those are disclosures about how the system is intended to operate, not evidence of concealed access to funds or a credential request. The material therefore supports a technology-focused explanation whose stated risk premise is decentralization and automatic execution, even if viewers should independently assess whether those claims hold in practice.

citations.quote: The code containing all the logic of the contract is placed on the blockchain network.
Hence there is no center can be hacked.
So even the creators can not cancel or change conditions

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited slot prices and partner placements describe the advertised operation, but they do not establish deception, hidden access, or an actual loss. The reference also concedes that the records do not verify the projected figures or completed payments. A stated mathematical projection and an explanation of automated distribution are not, by themselves, proof that the creator misrepresented the system.

citations.quote: Each payment is always immediately send to wallet of one of the participants.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical description does not neutralize the economic claims. The presentation says participants receive income when partners occupy positions and claims that income is unlimited through reinvestment. Its security language addresses control of code, not whether participants can actually obtain the promised returns or whether later participants fund earlier ones.

citations.quote: The first partner takes a place below you, a 100% payout instantly credited to your personal wallet.
Thus through reinvestments from each slot can be unlimited.

opening.argument: The material is structured as an operational tutorial: it defines decentralization, explains the X3 and X4 layouts, walks through placement and reinvestment, and describes how upgrades and transfers are supposed to work. The X3 and X4 diagrams are consistent with that instructional purpose, showing positions under a participant rather than showing a completed transaction or an identifiable victim. Explaining a mechanism, including its terminology and flow, is not the same as certifying that every projected result will occur. On the supplied record, the strongest characterization is an educational demonstration of a smart-contract-based matrix model.

citations.quote: What does decentralized mean? What are the benefits for you for such marketing created with a smart contract?
In the X3 program below you is one line in three places.
Forsage X4 In parallel with X3 you have the X4 program running.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the subject a matrix and describing ETH-denominated slots does not show that the video is soliciting a fraudulent payment. The opening relies on the mechanics it is trying to teach, while the cited material contains no verified transaction, named victim, or demonstrated failure. Even the projected amount is presented within an explanation of how the model is calculated, not as evidence of a completed outcome.

citations.quote: For example, in the first week you went through a circle of the first level

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely neutral instruction. The tutorial tells viewers how many slots to activate, recommends a starting amount, urges partners to do the same, and describes income from invited partners. Those calls to participate make the instruction promotional, while the claimed projection supplies a financial inducement rather than just technical education.

citations.quote: The most balanced option for the majority is to start with 3 slots of both programs at once.
Recommend that your partners do the same so they do not lose profits.

opening.argument: The record can also be read as promotion of access to a defined digital service rather than a conventional deposit-taking scheme. It describes slots, program levels, automated reinvestment, and payments routed to participant wallets; it does not show a request for passwords, identity documents, a bank transfer, or direct custody by an operator. The source expressly says payments go immediately to one participant's wallet. Whatever one thinks of the business model, the supplied evidence does not establish the missing mechanisms of credential theft, hidden custody, or a guaranteed personal payout to every viewer.

citations.quote: And in Forsage really all 100% goes to partners.
Each payment is always immediately send to wallet of one of the participants.
Each of two programs x3 and x4 has 12 slots, they all are identical and work in the same way.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the presence of ETH prices and referrals as conclusive, but those facts are compatible with a disclosed referral service or digital program. It does not identify a concealed fee, stolen credential, or operator-controlled wallet. The cited 100% payout is a claim about routing, and the reference itself acknowledges there is no independent verification of payments or figures.

citations.quote: 100% of your payment goes to the wallet of your higher pattern

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-credential point is beside the issue. The mechanism described is a paid matrix in which invited partners occupy positions below a participant and their payments can trigger wallet payouts. The presentation also says upgrading is necessary to continue receiving payment after reinvestment, so the evidence does show a recruitment-linked payment mechanism even without passwords or bank custody.

citations.quote: When you invite partners they take places under you.
To receive payment after reinvest you need to upgrade.
